title: Western Springs Pumping Station
geometryBasis: The mapped common south wall and north-side step constrain the 25.9 m connected envelope. The deeper eastern volume is the two-storey engine house. The western volume is the single-storey boiler wing.
sectionBasis: The heritage records identify red brick, dressed basalt quoins and openings, round-arched multi-pane windows, cornices, entrance steps, hipped roofs, and broad arched boiler-house doorways.
limitations: Wall and roof heights, window spacing and the connecting wall are approximate. The municipal illustration gives overall massing. The written heritage survey supplies opening and material details.
The current terrain remains unchanged. The DEM-derived approach and foundations give approximate vertical fit. The height of the now-demolished chimney is part of the historical record.
floorBasis: The public approach is used as the ground datum. The stone base extends below the original surface and the entrance steps reach the modest common floor rise.
